_README: Pre-season signal that the official FPL API does not carry. FPL only ingests competitive
Premier League matches: its /fixtures/ endpoint returns exactly 380 league games with the
earliest kickoff on the GW1 date, every player's `form` is 0.0 until GW1 is played, and no
element field references friendlies. So none of this can be fetched by engine/fetch.py -
it is entered by hand and consumed by engine/preseason.py.
Team-level friendly RESULTS are published free (premierleague.com). Player-level MINUTES -
the signal that actually matters for FPL - are paywalled (Fantasy Football Scout's tracker
is Chief Scout members only), so `players[].minutes` is left null unless someone fills it
in from a source they have access to. Never invent these numbers; a null is honest and is
handled, a guess silently corrupts every downstream score.
players[] fields, all optional:
minutes / possible_minutes -> pre-season minutes share, blended into the reliability term.
Use for 'is this player nailed on', which is the main thing
pre-season is good for.
availability  0.0-1.0       -> multiplier for a fitness/rotation risk FPL has not yet
flagged. Ignored once FPL sets chance_of_playing_next_round,
which is a harder source and wins.
note / source               -> provenance. Required for anything that moves a number.
Friendly goals and assists are deliberately NOT scored. Pre-season output is a famously weak
predictor - weak opposition, trialists, experimental XIs - while minutes are informative.
context: The 2026 World Cup finished ~33 days before GW1. Players who went deep are expected to get
roughly three weeks off, putting some back in club training only around 10-12 August - under
two weeks before the 21 August deadline. Eight clubs also changed manager this summer, so
last season's minutes are a weaker guide to this season's XI than usual.
2026-08-02 refresh: the World Cup lay-off predicted in the note above is now confirmed for named
players rather than generic. Bruno Fernandes had still not rejoined Man Utd pre-season training in
late July - United granted their Portuguese contingent an extra week beyond the standard World Cup
extension - and Crystal Palace listed Munoz among a post-World Cup group still to be integrated.
FPL has flagged neither: both read status=a with chance_of_playing_next_round null and empty news.
That is exactly the case the availability field exists for, and FPL's own rating wins the moment
it sets one.
5 Aug: the friendly programme is into its informative phase - clubs field closer to first-choice XIs in their final one or two warm-ups, and the deep World
Cup runners rejoin club training around 10-12 August. Man City v Arsenal (FA Community Shield,
16 Aug) is a competitive fixture five days before the deadline and carries real injury risk for
assets at both clubs.
8 Aug: the big penultimate round is played (19 results on 8 Aug alone). Player-level minutes
remain paywalled, so these still cannot be scored - only recorded. World Cup returnees are due
back in club training around 10-12 August, so the editorial availability flags on Saka, Rice,
B.Fernandes and Munoz should be re-checked next run and dropped as soon as FPL publishes real
chance_of_playing values, which override them automatically.
Man City v Arsenal (FA Community Shield, 16 Aug) is competitive football five days before the
deadline and is the highest-impact injury risk for Arsenal assets.
8 Aug (transfer): Bruno Guimaraes has agreed a move from Newcastle to Arsenal and FPL has NOT
ingested it - the pool still reads NEW. This is the case `moved_to` exists for. FPL lags real
transfers by days during a window, and until it catches up every team-derived term is computed
against the wrong club, including the three-per-club limit, which can silently produce an
illegal squad. Check the window for further moves each run rather than trusting the pool's club.
8 Aug transfer audit: cross-checked every reported 2026 summer PL move against the live pool.
FPL is up to date on all of them except Bruno Guimaraes - Rogers, Lacroix, Welbeck, J.Henderson,
Elliot Anderson, Barco, Quenda, Emegha, Palestra, Manzambi, Joao Gomes, Garnacho, Victor Munoz,
M.Sangare, Trafford, Norgaard, Hornicek, Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, van Hecke, Robertson, Senesi
and Dubravka all carry the correct club. Also checked the mirror failure - players who left the
league but linger in the pool: 7 are marked status=u (loans and departures) and all are correctly
zeroed by chance_of_playing=0, so none can be selected. No top-40-owned player carries any news.
Beware surname matching when repeating this: Ibrahim vs Mamadou Sangare, Daniel vs Victor Munoz,
Dean vs Jordan Henderson and Beto vs Joao Gomes are different footballers. Match on element_id.
11 Aug: FPL has ingested the Bruno Guimaraes move (pool now reads ARS), so his moved_to override
is retired - the mechanism stays for the next one. New injury: Mukiele (SUN) is FPL-flagged at 75%
with a knock, which now feeds the model directly and outranks any editorial guess. The World Cup
returnee window (10-12 Aug) has NOT yet produced FPL ratings - Saka, Rice, Merino, B.Fernandes,
Munoz and Bruno G. all still read status=a with chance_of_playing null, so the editorial 0.7/0.75
flags are still doing the work. Re-check daily from here; this is the last soft spot before the
deadline.
16 Aug (5 days out): friendly programme is essentially complete - 12 and 15 Aug rounds recorded,
these were the final warm-ups and therefore the most first-choice XIs of the summer. Still not
scored: player minutes stay paywalled, so the closest-to-informative matches of the calendar are
the ones we can least read. This is the single biggest remaining gap in the model.
The FA Community Shield (Arsenal v Man City, Cardiff) is TODAY and unplayed at time of writing -
competitive football five days before the deadline, with Raya and Gabriel (the recommended
captain) both Arsenal. Re-check FPL for new flags after it finishes.
World Cup returnee flags STILL unresolved with 5 days to go: Saka, Rice, Merino, B.Fernandes,
Munoz and Bruno G. all read status=a, chance_of_playing null. The editorial 0.7/0.75 flags have
now been carrying that call for two weeks unverified - treat as the weakest input in the model.
17 Aug - COMMUNITY SHIELD READ (Arsenal 3-0 Man City, 16 Aug). The first competitive XIs of the
season and by far the best selection evidence we have had; it is worth more than the entire
friendly programme above.
Arsenal XI: Raya; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Odegaard, Lewis-Skelly, Guimaraes;
Madueke, Havertz, Tzolis. Subs incl. Saka, Rice, Merino, Eze, Zubimendi, Gyokeres.
Man City XI: Donnarumma; Khusanov, Dias, Gvardiol, O'Reilly; Kovacic, Anderson, Semenyo;
Foden, Haaland, Doku. Subs incl. Guehi, Marmoush, Cherki, Grealish.
Readings: Raya and Gabriel both started and kept a clean sheet in a 3-0 win, which supports the
Gabriel captaincy. Bruno Guimaraes started - flag retired. Saka, Rice and Merino were all benched
- they are FIT (named in a competitive squad) but not starting, so their flags are kept and are
now observation rather than speculation. Note this cuts both ways: a manager may rest returnees
for a Shield and start them in GW1, so treat as strong evidence, not proof.
Maresca confirmed in charge of Man City, so the MCI 0.90 flag stands. Guehi was on the City
BENCH, which is worth remembering if he is ever considered.
17 Aug DATA BUG: the entry labelled 'Saka' carried element_id 17, which is Merino. Saka (id 12)
was therefore going completely unflagged while Merino silently took the haircut meant for him.
validate() did not catch it because it only checked that the id EXISTED in the pool, not that it
matched the web_name - a transposed id points at a real player, just the wrong one. validate()
now compares the name too. Fixed: Saka -> id 12, Merino given his own entry at id 17.

_clubs_README: Club-level uncertainty, applied to every player at the club and compounded with
any per-player flag. A new manager is the main case: last season's minutes stop
being a reliable guide to this season's XI, and nothing in the FPL API expresses
that. Eight clubs changed manager in summer 2026, so this list is not complete -
add the rest as their pre-season XIs become readable.
`availability` here is a judgment call, not a measurement. 0.90 is a deliberately
modest 10% haircut on minutes certainty: enough to break a tie against an
equivalent player at a settled club, not enough to exclude a genuinely better one.
Tighten it towards 0.80 if pre-season line-ups look heavily rotated, and remove
the entry once the new XI is established and FPL's own data reflects it.

clubs.note: Enzo Maresca replaced Pep Guardiola on a three-year deal, ending a decade under one manager. Squad roles, set-piece duties and rotation patterns are all unproven, and last season's minutes were earned under a different system.
clubs.source: Sky Sports / Al Jazeera, June 2026 - Maresca appointed Man City manager

friendlies_note: Partial from 2026-07-30 onward - only fixtures whose date could be attributed to a source are listed. Team-level results are decorative anyway: nothing in engine/score.py reads this array. Friendly RESULTS are not scored, by design (see _README). It is kept as provenance for the player and club entries below, which are the parts that move numbers.
notes_not_scored: Joao Pedro (CHE): hat-trick in nine minutes plus an assist vs Western Sydney, 2026-07-29, and public praise from Alonso. Deliberately moves NO number - friendly goals are a weak predictor and the _README rules them out. Recorded so a future run doesn't mistake the silence for absence.
Mbeumo (MUN): scored twice off the bench in United's 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid, and has been involved throughout pre-season. Same rule - not scored, recorded as context.
Mateus Fernandes (TOT) was the 'Fernandes' rested with calf fatigue in the 2026-07-30 report, NOT Bruno Fernandes. Logged because the name collision is an easy and expensive mistake to repeat.
